label: thm:strong-multiplicativity
title: Strong multiplicativity
html:
Let G be a non-commutative formal group. Its comultiplication is an algebra homomorphism: for all x, y \in \mathrm{Dist}(G),

  \Delta(xy) \;=\; \Delta(x) \cdot \Delta(y)

component-wise, where \Delta is the comultiplication on \mathrm{Dist}(G). This is the strong multiplicativity of \Delta, and it is the property that lets the comultiplication — which encodes the gauge connection in the QOU framework — survive the passage from characteristic p to characteristic 0.

What is established here, and what is cited. The identity above holds for any object of the structure by definition: it is the defining compatibility axiom, restated. The substantive result of [fred2005], Theorem 4.12 — that the constructed \mathrm{Dist}(G) obtained by integrating the skew-Poisson structure satisfies it, and that the property is preserved under the Gröbner--Shirshov deformation at every filtration degree — is a strictly stronger statement. It is cited, not re-derived, and it does not follow from the identity above. Expressing "at every filtration degree" requires a filtered-deformation structure this model does not carry.
